post_commit_telemetry.description: HTTP handlers emit ordinary audit after mutation; stdout/file/SQLite/PostgreSQL request sinks remain optional/bounded asynchronous telemetry. Some CLI/startup operations only print or trace. security_outbox has a bounded read API, but no production dispatcher with persisted consumer cursor exists.

operator_output.description: One-shot operator command prints bounded result or report; it does not dispatch durable authority events. Existing outbox rows are separate from that output.

unsupported_no_delivery.description: No corresponding gateway-owned operation/delivery is shipped in this mode; required authority-event delivery cannot be inferred from provider audit or future plans.

journaled_dispatch.description: Cluster mode (migration 21): the evidence row is journaled in authority_event_journal in its own transaction under its own event_id, reserving one unit of bounded capacity; a full journal refuses the mutation and evicts nothing. Since migration 26 an admin session grant takes two units, one held for its withdrawal, and a withdrawal spends that unit and is never refused for capacity. With AUTHORITY_EVENT_SINK=log or file, one leased dispatcher reads the journal after a fenced, persisted cursor in bounded batches, delivers authority_event_delivery.v1 records whose actor and resource are keyed safe references, and advances the cursor only after the sink accepted: at least once, deduplicated on (authority_id, event_id). Retention prunes only delivered rows past AUTHORITY_EVENT_RETENTION_HOURS and never an evidence row. With AUTHORITY_EVENT_SINK=none nothing is delivered, and AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE_DURABILITY=required refuses to start such a replica. Since migration 24 the record also carries the actor's kind and auth mode and a keyed reference to a principal's issuer, each null where the evidence row recorded none. It is still not the proposed authority_event.v1: the subject reference is not issuer-scoped, actors without an issuer and rows committed before migration 24 cannot name one, and the operation identity is not caller-bound.

standalone_cursor_dispatch.description: Standalone mode has no journal. Each SQLite store that owns an authority (the token database, and the Connections database for Connection, local-secret and catalog evidence) is its own evidence authority, with a persisted authority_id in its authority_event_state table, written once. Its evidence tables' AUTOINCREMENT sequences are commit order within each table, and each table is delivered after its own cursor in the same file's authority_event_cursors (token database open-time schema; Connections schema migration 14). With AUTHORITY_EVENT_SINK=log or file, one task reads at most 100 rows after each cursor, projects them into authority_event_delivery.v1 records whose actor and resource are keyed safe references under that store's authority_id, offers them to the sink, and only then advances the cursor by compare-and-set in an IMMEDIATE transaction: at least once, deduplicated on (authority_id, event_id), retried with the 0.5 s to 60 s backoff, never skipping a row, and stalling a table at a row it cannot project. The record carries no shared security revision (null), no token revision (null before and after) and, for a re-encryption batch, no secret (a fixed local-secret-store reference on the maintenance axis). Nothing is delivered inside the authority's transaction, and evidence is never pruned. With AUTHORITY_EVENT_SINK=none nothing is delivered, and AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE_DURABILITY=required refuses to start. Not authority_event.v1, for the same reasons as journaled_dispatch.

groups.boundary: persist_policy_mutation -> PolicyControlPlane::commit -> commit_policy_in / postgres_documents::commit_in; active row lock and expected ETag guard; document/history, shared revision, active pointer, security_outbox and one document_change_evidence row commit together. Discovery acceptance invokes commit_policy_in inside its suggestion transaction, so its evidence row shares that transaction. An empty or oversized actor, or an action that cannot describe the resource, is refused before anything is written; an evidence insert failure rolls the whole commit (and an acceptance's transition) back.
groups.record: Immutable policy_documents retain actor subject, diff/action, document ETag and version; security_outbox retains committed revision/from/to. document_change_evidence (migration 23) has no foreign key and holds one row per committed change: operation code, event/operation UUIDs, actor kind/subject/issuer/auth mode, prior/new version, the outbox row's shared revision and database-clock committed_at. Stale ETag, lost initialize race and refused acceptance write none.
groups.actor: The handler names the operation and passes the authenticated principal: subject (1 to 4096 bytes), issuer (1 to 4096 bytes, or none) and auth mode (session_cookie, bearer_token, service_token, client_certificate), the principal bounds. The import's activation is the system actor import-standalone with auth mode system. No keyed safe actor reference yet. The kind vocabulary is migration 23's own, not migration 24's: a service-token caller is actor_kind principal with auth mode service_token (migration 24 records actor_kind service_token), and the issuer is stored as the principal carried it, not in canonical form.
groups.identity: Generated event_id and operation_id UUIDs; operation code policy.publish, policy.rollback, policy.rule.create/update/delete/reorder or policy.suggestion.accept (configuration.import for the import); prior/new version and shared security revision equal to the outbox row's; exactly one row per activated version. operation_id is minted per commit, not bound to a client idempotency key; a lost response is reconciled from the version's evidence row.
groups.follow_up: PR2 follow-up: caller-bound operation identity at the commit boundary and keyed safe actor references, and the actor columns aligned with migration 24's (service_token kind, canonical issuer) before the rows are journaled. Journal document_change_evidence (it is not a migration 21 journal source yet) so the dispatcher delivers it, with the journal's capacity reservation in the same transaction.
groups.test_claim: PostgreSQL-gated regression anchors for the transactional document evidence. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract, delivery or retention.

groups.boundary: persist_to_file writes temporary file and renames; reload swaps runtime; append_policy_version_after_commit writes a separately configured SQLite history database afterward.
groups.record: Policy file survives successful persistence; SQLite policy history is separate and may fail after success. Neither optional telemetry nor the separate history write is an atomic authority/evidence boundary.
groups.actor: History has actor_user_id if append succeeds; file has none.
groups.identity: File semantic ETag; independent SQLite history version. No common authoritative revision or operation ID across commits.
groups.follow_up: PR4 depends on #242: introduce/reuse its crash-safe standalone revision ledger, bind file digest + activation + history + evidence, recover interrupted activation; keep required-durability policy mutations unsupported until proven.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: File watcher/SIGHUP -> reload_policy_from_file_locked validates file and replaces process snapshot, then emits reload telemetry; it does not append policy history.
groups.record: Operator-owned file and process snapshot; no atomic activation/evidence record.
groups.actor: Reload event does not authenticate an editing operator.
groups.identity: No ledger revision binds the accepted file to activation or identifies the operation.
groups.follow_up: #242/#425 PR4 must route watcher, SIGHUP and startup activation through the same ledger as admin publication; testing only admin endpoints is insufficient.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: Config rejects POLICY_FILE in PostgreSQL mode; replicas install authoritative database revisions.
groups.record: No file authority is supported in this mode.
groups.actor: Not applicable.
groups.identity: Security revision belongs to database publication, not a file reload.
groups.follow_up: Keep this operation refused; do not introduce a local file authority fallback.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: register_tools_via_control_plane -> commit_tools -> shared document transaction with CAS, name reservations, immutable version, pointer, revision, outbox and one document_change_evidence row. The first-boot seed and the import's activation use the same transaction.
groups.record: tool_documents retain actor subject and action/diff with version and ETag; the outbox row and the non-cascading document_change_evidence row (migration 23) commit with them. A later failed local install does not undo that commit, and its evidence row keeps describing the committed version. A tool name another lane holds writes none.
groups.actor: Authenticated principal kind/subject/issuer/auth mode for registration; the system actors bootstrap (first-boot seed) and import-standalone (import), auth mode system. No keyed safe actor reference yet. Same migration 23 vocabulary as policy: a service-token caller is actor_kind principal, and the issuer is not canonicalized.
groups.identity: Generated event/operation UUIDs, tools.publish (configuration.import for the import), prior/new tools version and the outbox row's shared security revision; operation_id minted per commit, no client-bound operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2 follow-up: caller-bound operation identity and keyed safe actor references, shared with policy; preserve tool-name locks and committed-but-not-locally-installed semantics. Journal the rows for dispatch, as for policy.
groups.test_claim: PostgreSQL-gated regression anchors for the transactional document evidence. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract, delivery or retention.

groups.boundary: Admin publication calls registry replace_local_definitions_with_persist with fs::write, then installs definitions. File watcher/SIGHUP reloads definitions into the registry and emits loaded telemetry without a history transaction.
groups.record: Tools file holds current document; no durable publication history/evidence transaction.
groups.actor: Authenticated actor only in separate telemetry.
groups.identity: Current tools ETag; no durable operation or history revision.
groups.follow_up: #242/#425 PR4: include tools-file writes and watcher/startup paths in ledger integration; current fs::write must not be described as an atomic evidence transaction.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: policy_tests_put_endpoint -> PostgresPolicyTestSuiteStore::commit -> postgres_documents::commit_in over migration 29's policy_test_suite_versions and policy_test_suite_active; active row lock and expected ETag (If-Match, or Initialize for If-None-Match: *) guard; immutable version, shared revision, active pointer, security_outbox (resource_type policy_tests) and one document_change_evidence row commit together. An empty or oversized actor is refused before anything is written; an evidence insert failure rolls the whole commit back.
groups.record: Immutable policy_test_suite_versions retain actor subject, a counts-only diff summary, the suite and its ETag (the suite's semantic digest); security_outbox retains the revision and from/to versions. document_change_evidence (widened by migration 29) holds one row per committed write with action policy_tests.publish and resource_type policy_tests, event/operation UUIDs, actor kind/subject/issuer/auth mode, prior/new version and the outbox row's shared revision. A stale ETag, an existing suite under If-None-Match: * and a lost initialize race write none.
groups.actor: The handler passes the authenticated principal: subject, issuer (or none) and auth mode, in migration 23's actor vocabulary, as for policy. No keyed safe actor reference yet.
groups.identity: Generated event_id and operation_id UUIDs; operation code policy_tests.publish; prior/new suite version and the outbox row's shared security revision; exactly one row per stored version. The proposed event names the suite as a policy resource on its own policy_tests revision axis, since its versions are not policy versions.
groups.follow_up: Shared with policy: caller-bound operation identity and keyed safe actor references, and journaling document_change_evidence for dispatch.
groups.test_claim: PostgreSQL-gated regression anchors for the transactional document evidence. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract, delivery or retention.

groups.boundary: policy_tests_put_endpoint -> SqlitePolicyTestSuiteStore::commit: one IMMEDIATE SQLite transaction in the policy history database reads the newest version, re-checks the precondition and appends the next one.
groups.record: policy_test_suite_versions retains the actor subject, creation time, suite, ETag and case count of every version; there is no separate evidence record of who made the change beyond that subject.
groups.actor: actor_user_id (subject) on the version row only; no issuer or auth mode.
groups.identity: Suite ETag (its semantic digest) and the SQLite version number. No shared revision or operation ID.
groups.follow_up: #242/#425: bind standalone suite writes into the crash-safe standalone revision ledger with the policy writes; keep required-durability suite writes refused until then.
groups.test_claim: Existing behavior regression anchors only; these tests do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: PostgresConnectionStore::create/replace refuse an actor the evidence cannot record exactly (ChangeActor::is_recordable) before opening a transaction, then lock shared Connection state, check collection/object CAS, write records, credential bindings, immutable version, shared revision and outbox, append one connection_change_evidence row carrying the outbox row's shared revision (connection.create, or connection.replace plus credential.binding_change under the same operation_id when the replacement advances the credential revision), journal each row, and commit once. An evidence insert or journal append failure rolls the whole change back and is reported as a store failure (503), never as a conflict or validation problem; a full journal refuses the change with 503. Credential/TLS revisions derive from replacement; an identical replace commits nothing and records nothing.
groups.record: connection_versions actor/diff and outbox from/to are atomic; that history cascades when the Connection is deleted. Since migration 28, connection_change_evidence (no foreign key) keeps one row per committed create and replace, and one credential.binding_change row per replacement that advances the credential revision: the actor, action, event/operation UUIDs, revision_axis (connection, or credential for the binding change), the revision before and after on that axis (none before a create; 0 before a binding change means no credential authority was configured), the outbox row's shared revision and database-clock committed_at. No specification, endpoint, header name, binding, bound secret ID or locator. Stale ETag, collection conflict, capacity, a lost race, an unrecordable actor and an identical replace write no row. Connections created or replaced before migration 28 have no such rows; nothing is backfilled.
groups.actor: The authenticated principal the admin create and put endpoints pass through the control plane and ManagedConnectionStore as a ChangeActor (ChangeActor::from_principal), committed with the change: actor_user_id (the subject, 1 to 4096 bytes), actor_kind (principal or service_token), actor_auth_mode and the canonical actor_issuer of a principal that has one (1 to 4096 bytes). connection_documents still records the subject while the Connection exists. A keyed safe actor reference exists only in what is delivered.
groups.identity: Generated event_id and operation_id UUIDs per store call (not bound to a client idempotency key); a credential-changing replacement's two rows share its operation_id and shared revision. Connection ID, the revision transition on the row's axis, shared revision equal to the outbox row's, database-clock committed_at. A lost replace response is reconciled by the row naming the new version, and a retry with the old ETag is a conflict that writes nothing; a lost create response is reconciled by the Connection's create row, and a blind retry creates a second Connection with its own row.
groups.follow_up: PR2 follow-up: carry a caller-bound operation identity to the store and derive an issuer-scoped subject reference, so the delivered record can become authority_event.v1. Delivery journals each row in the change's transaction and dispatches it as authority_event_delivery.v1: connection.create and connection.replace on the connection axis, credential.binding_change on the credential axis with the Connection as its resource (v1 names a credential_binding resource, which the evidence cannot reference without a binding identifier it deliberately omits). AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE_DURABILITY=required makes a configured sink mandatory and admits this row; nothing qualifies it yet.
groups.test_claim: PostgreSQL-gated regression anchors for the transactional create, replace and credential binding change evidence and its journaled delivery: the actor recorded, refusals and lost races writing nothing, rollback on a failed evidence insert or journal append, a full journal refused with 503, survival after delete and restart, and binding and secret material absent. They do not certify the proposed authority_event.v1 contract.

groups.boundary: SqliteConnectionStore::create/replace refuse an actor the evidence cannot record exactly (ChangeActor::is_recordable) before any other work, then run one IMMEDIATE transaction on the CONNECTIONS_SQLITE_PATH database: write the record and bindings, append connection_change_evidence rows (connection.create; connection.replace, plus credential.binding_change under the same operation_id when the credential revision advances) and commit once. The control plane publishes its runtime snapshot only after that commit. An evidence insert failure rolls the whole change back and is reported as a store failure (503), never as a validation problem or conflict; an identical replace commits and records nothing.
groups.record: Current records and revisions are atomic. The same database's connection_change_evidence table (Connections schema migration 12, no foreign key) keeps one append-only row per committed create, replace and credential-axis change: actor (subject, kind, auth mode and, for a principal that has one, canonical issuer, with the same pairing CHECK as PostgreSQL migration 24 and every column required), action, event/operation UUIDs, Connection ID, the revision before and after on the action's axis (connection_revision; credential_revision for credential.binding_change), a commit-ordered sequence and the change's own committed_at. No specification, endpoint, binding or bound secret ID. Rows are never pruned, and import-standalone does not carry them.
groups.actor: The authenticated principal the admin endpoints pass through the control plane and the managed-store adapter as a ChangeActor, committed with the change: the subject (1 to 4096 bytes), actor_kind (principal or service_token), actor_auth_mode and the canonical actor_issuer of a principal that has one (1 to 4096 bytes). A keyed safe actor reference is absent.
groups.identity: Generated event_id/operation_id UUIDs per store call (not bound to a client idempotency key), Connection ID, prior/new revision per axis, store sequence and the process-clock committed_at (the record's updated_at). Standalone mode has no shared security revision and no database clock.
groups.follow_up: PR4 follow-up: a caller-bound operation identity at the store. Delivered from this same database since Connections schema migration 14 (standalone_cursor_dispatch), with no audit-database dual write; a credential.binding_change is delivered as the Connection's, on the credential axis. Catalog/overlay publication in this database is its own row (catalog_standalone). Issuer, actor kind and auth mode are recorded.
groups.test_claim: Standalone regression anchors for the create/replace/credential-change evidence in the Connections database's own transactions: forced insert failure and rollback, restart, refused changes and unrecordable actors, migration onto an existing database, the actor CHECKs pinned to PostgreSQL migration 24, and the admin endpoints recording the authenticated principal with its issuer. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: PostgresConnectionStore::delete refuses an actor the evidence cannot record exactly (ChangeActor::is_recordable: an empty or oversized subject or issuer, or an issuer on an actor that has none) before opening a transaction, then locks shared Connection state and the record, checks ETag and dependencies, appends the outbox tombstone to_version=0 and one connection_change_evidence row carrying the same shared revision, releases names, deletes the parent and commits once. An evidence insert failure rolls the whole delete back.
groups.record: Outbox tombstone unchanged; connection_documents and bindings cascade. connection_change_evidence (migration 16) has no foreign key, so it survives the cascade; it holds identifiers, revisions and the actor only. Stale ETag, dependency, missing record and lost race write no row.
groups.actor: The deleting principal as the admin endpoint builds it from the authenticated Principal (ChangeActor::from_principal), committed with the delete and retained after it: actor_user_id (the subject, 1 to 4096 bytes, the principal bound) and, since migration 24, actor_kind (principal or service_token), actor_auth_mode (the audit auth mode) and actor_issuer (the canonical issuer of a principal that has one, 1 to 4096 bytes). Rows committed before migration 24 record none of the three. No credential, session, role or email; a keyed safe actor reference exists only in what is delivered.
groups.identity: Generated event_id and operation_id UUIDs, Connection ID, prior version, shared security revision equal to the tombstone's revision, database-clock committed_at. operation_id is minted per store call, not bound to a client idempotency key; a lost response is reconciled by the Connection's evidence row, and a blind retry is NotFound.
groups.follow_up: PR2 follow-up: carry a caller-bound operation identity to the store and derive an issuer-scoped subject reference, so the delivered record can become authority_event.v1. Issuer, actor kind and auth mode are recorded since migration 24. Delivery (PR3) journals each row in the delete's transaction and dispatches it as authority_event_delivery.v1 behind a persisted cursor; AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE_DURABILITY=required makes a configured sink mandatory and admits this row; nothing qualifies it yet.
groups.test_claim: PostgreSQL-gated regression anchors for the transactional deletion evidence and its journaled delivery: commit order, crash redelivery under the same event IDs, retention floors and capacity refusal. They do not certify the proposed authority_event.v1 contract.

groups.boundary: SqliteConnectionStore::delete refuses an actor the evidence cannot record exactly (ChangeActor::is_recordable), then in one IMMEDIATE transaction checks bindings, ETag and dependencies, appends one connection_change_evidence row (connection.delete), deletes the record, whose children cascade, and commits once. An evidence insert failure rolls the delete back and is reported as a store failure (503).
groups.record: connection_change_evidence (no foreign key) keeps the deletion's actor (subject, kind, auth mode and, for a principal that has one, canonical issuer, with the same pairing CHECK as PostgreSQL migration 24 and every column required), action, event/operation UUIDs, Connection ID and prior connection revision with no successor after the record, bindings, catalogs and status have cascaded, beside the record's earlier create/replace rows. Stale ETag, dependency, missing record and an unrecordable actor write no row.
groups.actor: The authenticated principal passed through the managed-store adapter as a ChangeActor, the same one the PostgreSQL store records: subject (1 to 4096 bytes), actor_kind, actor_auth_mode and canonical actor_issuer, committed with the delete and retained after it.
groups.identity: Generated event_id/operation_id UUIDs, Connection ID, prior revision, store sequence and process-clock committed_at. A lost delete response is reconciled from the Connection's evidence rows; a blind retry is NotFound and records nothing.
groups.follow_up: PR4 follow-up: a caller-bound operation identity. Delivered from this same database since Connections schema migration 14 (standalone_cursor_dispatch); standalone mode has no journal. Issuer, actor kind and auth mode are recorded.
groups.test_claim: Standalone regression anchors for the transactional deletion evidence: survival of the cascade and a restart, refused deletes, forced insert failure and rollback. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: MCP/OpenAPI replacements and overlay updates share the Connection-state transaction and revision/CAS checks; entries, reservations, dependencies, outbox and one catalog_change_evidence row commit together. Registration, refresh and overlay put/delete all reach the OpenAPI replacement. An actor evidence cannot record exactly (an empty or oversized subject or issuer, or an issuer on a service token) is refused before the transaction opens; an evidence insert failure rolls the publication back.
groups.record: Current catalog/overlay rows keep their actor's subject and are still replaced or cascaded. catalog_change_evidence (migration 23, with migration 25's actor columns) has no foreign key and keeps one row per publication: action, event/operation UUIDs, the whole actor, Connection ID, prior/new catalog revision, the overlay revision the catalog was compiled from, the outbox row's shared revision and committed_at. A stale catalog or overlay revision, a conflict or a limit writes none.
groups.actor: Every catalog writer is an admin endpoint, which builds the ChangeActor from the authenticated Principal; the store records it whole, as Connection deletion does: actor_user_id (the subject, 1 to 4096 bytes, the principal bound), actor_kind, actor_auth_mode and, for a principal that has one, the canonical actor_issuer, in migration 25's columns under migration 24's pairing CHECK. They survive replacement and Connection deletion. Rows committed before this build record none of the three new columns, and nothing is backfilled. A keyed safe actor reference is still absent.
groups.identity: Generated event/operation UUIDs; catalog.mcp.publish, catalog.openapi.publish, catalog.overlay.replace or catalog.overlay.delete, derived from the write; the catalog revision transition of the connection_catalog outbox row (its 0 stored as NULL), overlay revision and shared revision. Catalog revisions restart when a Connection re-enters a managed kind, so evidence is ordered by security revision. No client-bound operation ID.
groups.follow_up: PR2 follow-up: carry a caller-bound operation identity to the Connection store's catalog writers; a scheduled refresh, if one is added, records a system actor, which the table can now express. Catalogs removed by a Connection kind change are connection.replace evidence. Journal catalog_change_evidence (not a migration 21 journal source yet) so the dispatcher delivers it.
groups.test_claim: PostgreSQL-gated regression anchors for the transactional catalog evidence. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract, delivery or retention.

groups.boundary: SqliteConnectionStore::replace_mcp_catalog_expecting and replace_openapi_catalog_with_overlay_and_enum_values refuse an actor the evidence cannot record exactly (ChangeActor::is_recordable) before anything is read, then run one IMMEDIATE transaction on the CONNECTIONS_SQLITE_PATH database: check the Connection ETag and the catalog (for OpenAPI also the spec and overlay) revisions, write the catalog, its dependencies, the overlay and the enum values its compile resolved, append one catalog_change_evidence row and commit once. Registration, refresh and overlay put/delete all reach the OpenAPI replacement. The action is named by what the write did to the overlay, as the PostgreSQL writer names it: an overlay put is catalog.overlay.replace, an overlay delete catalog.overlay.delete, an MCP publication catalog.mcp.publish, and an OpenAPI registration or refresh (no overlay change, or only refreshed source reports) catalog.openapi.publish. The catalog services install the published catalog only after that commit. An evidence insert failure rolls the publication back and is reported as a store failure (503), never as a validation problem, a conflict or an invalid upstream response. Enum-value refreshes and status observations publish no catalog and write no row.
groups.record: Current catalog revisions, entries and dependencies and the overlay (with its last writer's subject) are replaced atomically. The same database's catalog_change_evidence table (Connections schema migration 13, no foreign key) keeps one append-only row per committed publication: actor (subject, kind, auth mode and, for a principal that has one, canonical issuer, with migration 12's bounds and pairing CHECK and every column required), action, event/operation UUIDs, Connection ID, the catalog revision before (none for a first catalog) and after, the overlay revision the published catalog was compiled from (0 for none; none for MCP), a commit-ordered sequence and the publication's own committed_at, under PostgreSQL migration 23's action vocabulary and revision CHECKs. No specification, digest, tool or resource name, definition, overlay document, source report, enum value, endpoint or binding. A stale Connection ETag, a stale catalog, spec or overlay revision, a mismatched compiled overlay revision, a bound, a kind mismatch and an unrecordable actor write none. Rows outlive the catalogs they replaced and the Connection whose deletion cascades the current ones; they are never pruned, and import-standalone does not carry them.
groups.actor: The authenticated principal the refresh, OpenAPI registration and overlay endpoints pass through the MCP and OpenAPI catalog services and the managed-store adapter as a ChangeActor, committed with the publication: the subject (1 to 4096 bytes), actor_kind (principal or service_token), actor_auth_mode and the canonical actor_issuer of a principal that has one (1 to 4096 bytes). A keyed safe actor reference is absent.
groups.identity: Generated event_id/operation_id UUIDs per store call (not bound to a client idempotency key), Connection ID, the catalog revision transition and compiled overlay revision, store sequence and the process-clock committed_at (the catalog's refreshed_at). Standalone mode has no shared security revision and no database clock; catalog revisions restart when a Connection re-enters a managed kind, so a Connection's rows are ordered by sequence.
groups.follow_up: PR4 follow-up: a caller-bound operation identity at the store. Delivered from this same database since Connections schema migration 14 (standalone_cursor_dispatch), with no audit-database dual write, on the catalog axis under a reference to the Connection's catalog; the compiled overlay revision stays in the row. Catalogs removed by a Connection kind change are connection.replace evidence (connection_standalone). Issuer, actor kind and auth mode are recorded.
groups.test_claim: Standalone regression anchors for the catalog and overlay publication evidence in the Connections database's own transactions: every action with three actor shapes, survival of replacement, Connection deletion and restart, refused and stale publications and unrecordable actors, forced insert failure and rollback with its store-failure classification, the migration onto an existing database, the CHECKs pinned to migration 12 and PostgreSQL migration 23, synthetic-marker exclusion, and the required-mode admin endpoints recording the authenticated principal. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: LocalSecretProvider create/rotate/delete and reencrypt_master_key_batch refuse an actor the evidence cannot record exactly (ChangeActor::is_recordable), then each runs one IMMEDIATE transaction in the Connections SQLite database that changes the envelope(s) and appends one connection_local_secret_change_evidence row before it commits; an evidence insert failure rolls the change back (ChangeEvidenceFailure, 503 from the admin API). Control-plane preflights and runtime publication surround the store call; the CLI executes one bounded batch per invocation.
groups.record: Current sealed record, version and timestamps; rotation replaces material and deletion removes it. connection_local_secret_change_evidence (Connections schema migration 12, no foreign key) keeps one append-only row per committed create, rotate, delete and non-empty re-encryption batch: actor (subject, kind, auth mode and, for a principal that has one, canonical issuer, with the same pairing CHECK as PostgreSQL migration 24 and every column required), action, event/operation UUIDs, the gateway-minted secret ID and its version before/after, or for a batch only how many envelopes it rewrote. Never the label, purpose, plaintext, ciphertext, nonce or key ID. Not found, purpose mismatch, dependency conflict and an empty batch write none.
groups.actor: Admin endpoints pass the authenticated principal as a ChangeActor: subject (1 to 4096 bytes), actor_kind, actor_auth_mode and canonical actor_issuer. The connection-secrets reencrypt command records the fixed label operator:connection-secrets-reencrypt as a system actor (kind and auth mode system, no issuer), which is not a named human.
groups.identity: Generated event/operation UUIDs per store call, the local secret ID with its version axis (no successor on delete), or the batch count in the maintenance shape with no revision, store sequence and process-clock committed_at (a rotation's rotated_at). The secret ID is an internal identifier; a delivered event would need a keyed reference for it.
groups.follow_up: PR4 follow-up: a caller-bound operation identity. Delivered from this same database since Connections schema migration 14 (standalone_cursor_dispatch), with a keyed reference for the secret ID; a re-encryption batch, which names no secret, is delivered on the maintenance axis under a fixed reference to the local-secret store. import-standalone does not carry these rows. Issuer, actor kind and auth mode are recorded.
groups.test_claim: Standalone regression anchors for the transactional local-secret evidence in the Connections database: forced insert failure and rollback of each change, restart, refused changes and unrecordable actors, synthetic-marker exclusion, the CLI's system actor and the admin endpoints recording the authenticated principal. They do not certify the proposed authority-event contract or delivery.

groups.boundary: Only with ADMIN_SESSION_MODE=standalone_memory, which configuration accepts only with STATE_BACKEND=sqlite. AdminSessions::issue validates the provider access token, then MemoryAdminSessionStore::grant admits one capability-digest entry to a bounded process-local map under its mutex; an admitted replacement removes the browser's prior session in the same critical section. Withdrawal is logout (AdminSessions::revoke, then MemoryAdminSessionStore::withdraw under the same mutex), the absolute or idle deadline, an access token the provider now rejects, an identity change, or a process restart, which discards the whole map. No database or file transaction is involved.
groups.record: No durable record. The entry (cookie digest, server-held access token, CSRF-token digest, absolute and idle deadlines, subject and issuer, random session ID) exists in memory only. The handler emits an admin_login.transaction audit event (phase, outcome, reason) after a grant or logout through the optional bounded audit sinks; implicit withdrawals emit none.
groups.actor: The granted principal's subject and issuer are held in memory only. The admin_login.transaction event carries no actor, session ID or principal, and logout is authentication-exempt and names no actor.
groups.identity: A random per-session UUID, exposed to later requests as Principal.session_id; it is not persisted, not on the grant or logout event, and gone after restart. No operation, event or revision identity.
groups.follow_up: #425: the standalone session authority is process-local memory by design, so no store exists that could own atomic evidence. AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE_DURABILITY=required refuses ADMIN_SESSION_MODE=standalone_memory at startup rather than relabel the post-change audit event as durable. Cluster mode's shared store records grant and withdrawal evidence in its own transactions (admin_session_postgres).

groups.boundary: Only with ADMIN_SESSION_MODE=cluster_postgres, which configuration accepts only with STATE_BACKEND=postgres (standalone_memory stays refused there). Beginning a login and granting a session first run the bounded expiry prune in a transaction of its own, so the journal's state row is the last row any admission locks. PostgresAdminSessionStore grant is then one transaction: a transaction-scoped advisory lock, the pending cookie login (live, unissued, FOR UPDATE), the capacity count, the replaced session's withdrawal with its evidence and journal rows, the session row (access token sealed under ADMIN_LOGIN_KEYRING), its grant evidence row and its journal row in one statement, then the login's issued marker; it commits once. Since migration 26 the grant statement takes two units of authority-event journal capacity, its own event's and one held for the session's withdrawal, only while both fit; when they do not, the grant rolls back and is answered 503. Logout (withdraw), a provider rejection or identity change (reject) and expiry (the bounded prune, per admission and in the admin_session_prune maintenance job, each in a transaction) each delete the session row, insert its withdrawal evidence row and journal it in one statement, spending the unit the grant held and checking no capacity, so a full journal never refuses a withdrawal. A failed evidence or journal write rolls the change back and is answered 503.
groups.record: admin_sessions rows (cookie digest, sealed token, CSRF-token digest, subject and issuer, database-clock absolute and idle deadlines) are runtime state that every withdrawal deletes. admin_session_evidence (migration 19) has no foreign key and outlives them: event and operation UUIDs, the random session ID, the action, a reason (issued, logout, replaced, rejected, expired), subject and issuer, the absolute deadline and database-clock committed_at; never the cookie, CSRF token, login binding or access token. Since migration 26 each row is journaled in authority_event_journal (source admin_session_evidence) in the statement that writes it, and authority_event_state.reserved_withdrawals holds one unit per session granted and not yet withdrawn; migration 26 journals the evidence committed before it and holds a unit for every session row then present. Moving the idle deadline on use writes no evidence, and an expiry is committed when the prune removes the row, not at the deadline.
groups.actor: The session's own principal (subject and issuer, as the provider validated them at issuance) on the grant and on its withdrawal. Logout is authentication-exempt and made by whoever presents the session cookie or the login binding; it names no other actor. A replaced withdrawal shares its operation_id with the replacement's grant. rejected and expired are system withdrawals on the provider's verdict and the database clock. No actor kind or auth mode is stored.
groups.identity: Generated event_id per row and operation_id per store call (a replacement's withdrawal and grant share one; a prune step uses one for its batch), the session's random UUID (Principal.session_id, never the cookie) and database-clock committed_at. UNIQUE (session_id, action) allows one grant and one withdrawal per session. No revision axis is stored, and operation_id is not bound to a client idempotency key.
groups.follow_up: Actor kind and auth mode (an expiry and a provider rejection are system withdrawals, but the evidence names only the session's subject, which the delivered record carries under actor.recorded with null kind, auth mode and issuer reference), an issuer-scoped subject reference, the withdrawal reason in the delivered record, and a caller-bound operation identity, before any authority_event.v1 projection. Delivery is the journaled dispatcher since migration 26: admin_session.grant and admin_session.withdraw on the session axis (revision 1 created by the grant, deleted by the withdrawal) with a null shared security revision. Holding a unit per grant so that withdrawals are never refused at capacity is the documented reversible default (docs/authority-evidence.md, Admin session withdrawals and journal capacity); required-durability mode is still not implemented.
